name: Classical NLP Models
description: Test your understanding of classic text processing techniques from TF-IDF and LDA to early neural architectures.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Inverse Document Frequency (IDF) term in TF-IDF?
options: To count total occurrences across sentences
To penalize words appearing in many documents
To generate dense vector representations
To capture contextual word order patterns
questions.explain: IDF scales down the weight of words that occur frequently across the entire corpus.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major limitation of classic Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF models?
options: They require labeled target data to run
They ignore word order and semantic meaning
They cannot handle numerical input features
They run exclusively on parallel GPU cores
questions.explain: Traditional Bag-of-Words models treat text as unstructured bags and miss sentence order and semantics.

questions.question: How is Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) categorized in text processing?
options: Supervised classification algorithm
Sequence-to-sequence translation model
Unsupervised topic modeling technique
Rule-based dependency parser framework
questions.explain: LDA discovers underlying topics across unstructured documents without human-provided labels.

questions.question: What human step is typically required after LDA extracts topic word distributions?
options: Calculating the cross-entropy loss value
Interpreting the word list to name the topic
Converting continuous tokens into integers
Re-indexing the document sparse matrices
questions.explain: LDA outputs representative word clusters which humans analyze to assign qualitative topic names.

questions.question: How can semantic clustering help improve traditional LDA topic models?
options: By enforcing strict word order dependencies
By replacing all multi-layer neural networks
By grouping synonyms using word embeddings
By converting text tokens into binary hashes
questions.explain: Grouping semantically related terms via embeddings mitigates the semantic blindness of LDA.

questions.question: Why is the phrase 'dog bit man' indistinguishable from 'man bit dog' in standard Bag-of-Words?
options: Word order is discarded in token frequency counts
Both sentences share the exact same sentiment label
Stopword removal strips out the nouns and verbs
Stemming reduces every word to an identical root
questions.explain: Bag-of-Words only counts word frequencies, entirely losing the sequential order of words.

questions.question: Which preprocessing step involves reducing words to their base dictionary forms?
options: Lemmatization
Quantization
Token pooling
Vector slicing
questions.explain: Lemmatization uses vocabulary and morphological analysis to return words to their base lemma.

questions.question: What is the primary formula component represented by df_x in TF-IDF calculations?
options: The total count of term x across one single document
The relative frequency rank of document x in corpus
The maximum length of all documents containing term x
The number of documents containing the specific term x
questions.explain: The document frequency df_x measures how many documents contain the term x.

questions.question: How do continuous word embeddings capture grammatical and semantic relations?
options: Through positional vector distance and arithmetic
Through sequential token parsing in tree layers
Through binary one-hot vocabulary representation
Through character-level deterministic regex matching
questions.explain: Embeddings place similar concepts close in vector space and allow semantic arithmetic operations.

questions.question: Which common NLP task involves assigning predefined categories like spam or non-spam to texts?
options: Information retrieval
Text classification
Sequence generation
Semantic paraphrasing
questions.explain: Categorizing texts into predefined buckets such as spam or ham is the task of text classification.
